m1.typescript: m1 static modules come first and the breakpoint follows the last one

e1.typescript: e1 a variable in a static module is refused

e2.typescript: e2 dynamic variables are filled and a missing one is refused

e3.typescript: e3 the lowest priority dynamic module is dropped first and a tie drops the later one

e4.typescript: e4 static modules are never dropped and a budget they exceed is refused

e5.typescript: e5 a prefix under the minimum gets no breakpoint

e6.typescript: e6 the cheapest model that meets the tier and the latency wins and ties go by name

e7.typescript: e7 only an identical static prefix can be reused

wrong-static-reversed.defect: puts the static modules in reverse order

wrong-breakpoint-after-all.defect: marks the breakpoint after the last block, dynamic ones included

wrong-variable-in-static-allowed.defect: accepts a variable inside a static module

wrong-missing-variable-blank.defect: replaces a missing variable with nothing

wrong-drop-highest-priority.defect: drops the module with the highest priority first

wrong-drop-tie-earlier.defect: drops the earlier of two modules with the same priority

wrong-over-budget-ignored.defect: returns a prompt over the budget when only static modules are left

wrong-minimum-exclusive.defect: needs more than the minimum for a breakpoint

wrong-minimum-one-low.defect: gives a breakpoint to a prefix one token under the minimum

wrong-model-tier-ignored.defect: ignores the capability tier the workload needs

wrong-model-tie-by-position.defect: breaks a price tie by list position and not by name

wrong-reuse-first-block-only.defect: compares only the first block of the prefix

wrong-reuse-needs-whole-prompt.defect: reuses nothing unless the whole prompt, dynamic blocks included, is identical
